title: OODA Loop
equation: Tempo Edge = Competitor Cycle Time ÷ Your Cycle Time
hook: The team that notices, decides, and acts fastest usually wins. Not the smartest one.
statement: Whoever goes from noticing to acting fastest sets the pace for everyone else.
explainer: Speed of adjusting beats getting any single decision perfect. When you move faster, your competitor is always reacting to a situation that's already changed.
sop: Break one recurring decision into Observe, Orient, Decide, Act.
Time each stage and find the slowest one.
Compare Your Cycle Time to your Competitor Cycle Time.
Pre-set rules so deciding takes minutes, not meetings.
Recheck weekly to see if your Tempo Edge is growing.
equation_example: Your competitor takes 60 hours to spot a change and respond. You take 20. 60 ÷ 20 = 3. Above 1 means you're setting the pace. Below 1 means you're the one always playing catch-up.
question: Write down how long it took you to respond to the last big change in your market.
closing_statement: Move before you feel fully ready.
caption:
Principle Nº 355: OODA Loop

The team that notices, decides, and acts fastest usually wins. Not the smartest one.

Whoever goes from noticing to acting fastest sets the pace for everyone else.

Your turn: Write down how long it took you to respond to the last big change in your market.
